classification.title: Budget Analyst I
classification.raw: Under general supervision, performs entry-level professional budget and financial analysis for city departments. Compiles and reconciles expenditure and revenue data, prepares variance reports and budget documents, reviews department requests for accuracy and policy compliance, and responds to inquiries from staff and the public. Requires knowledge of accounting principles, spreadsheet software and municipal budget processes; a bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, economics or a related field, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation.

classification.title: Engineering Technician I
classification.raw: Under direct supervision, performs entry-level technical engineering work supporting design, inspection and maintenance of streets, water and drainage infrastructure. Collects field measurements, reviews plans for completeness, prepares field reports and maintains project records. Works outdoors in varying conditions and follows site safety procedures. Requires an associate degree in engineering technology or related coursework, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation, and a valid driver's license.
competencies: Reads plans and field data accurately

classification.title: IT Support Analyst I
classification.raw: Provides first-level technical support for city employees. Responds to help desk tickets, sets up and troubleshoots computers, phones and accounts, documents solutions, and maintains equipment inventory. Follows security policies for access and data handling. Requires knowledge of desktop operating systems and basic networking; coursework in information technology or computer science, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation.
competencies: Explains technical issues in plain language

classification.title: Housing Program Specialist I
classification.raw: Assists residents in applying for city housing and community programs. Reviews applications for eligibility under program rules, maintains case files, explains requirements in person and by phone, coordinates with partner agencies, and protects confidential resident information. Requires strong written and verbal communication; a bachelor's degree in social work, human services, public administration or a related field, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation.
competencies: Works well with colleagues and residents

classification.title: Communications Specialist I
classification.raw: Writes and edits public information for the city, including web updates, social media posts, news releases and 311 knowledge articles. Verifies facts with departments, follows the city's style and accessibility standards, and monitors public channels for questions. Requires excellent writing skills; a bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, English, marketing or a related field, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation.
competencies: Uses the city's channels and tools

classification.title: Emergency Management Coordinator I
classification.raw: Supports emergency preparedness and court operations programs. Maintains emergency plans, contact lists and records, prepares briefings, helps staff exercises and the emergency operations center, and processes court documents according to procedure. Must follow established procedures under time pressure. Requires coursework in emergency management, criminal justice, public administration or a related field, or equivalent experience demonstrated through a Teaching City rotation.
competencies: Works well with colleagues and partners
